faqs.question: Do I need to hire a full architect to use ArchitectHire?
faqs.answer: No. That's the point — you can order a single consult, a set of renders, or drafting by the hour without committing to a full design engagement. Step up to a stamped set only when your project needs it.

faqs.question: How is this cheaper than a traditional firm?
faqs.answer: Most firms won't take work under a few thousand dollars because of minimum-fee overhead. We productize each service and match it to the right specialist — including offshore and freelance talent for unstamped work — so you pay only for what you order.

faqs.question: When do I actually need a licensed architect?
faqs.answer: Only for stamped, permit-ready deliverables, which must come from someone licensed in your jurisdiction. Everything else — renders, drafting, scans, feasibility, consults — needs no stamp and can be done by anyone on the platform.

faqs.question: How do payments work?
faqs.answer: Every service is priced up front and paid into escrow. Funds release to the specialist only as you approve milestones or the final files, so you're protected throughout.

faqs.question: Do I need finished drawings to order a render?
faqs.answer: No. A sketch, existing photos, or rough dimensions are enough to start — the artist will confirm what they need and quote accordingly. If you don't have plans yet, a 3D floor plan is a great first step.

faqs.question: How many revisions are included?
faqs.answer: Two rounds of revisions are included on every still. Additional rounds are billed transparently, and you'll see the cost before approving them.

faqs.question: Who owns the final images?
faqs.answer: You do. On final approval you receive full-resolution, print-ready files with usage rights for listings, submittals, and marketing.

faqs.question: Can the same specialist do my permit drawings too?
faqs.answer: Renders and drawings are separate services. Many clients start with a render, then engage a licensed architect for a stamped set — we keep those flows separate so you only pay for a stamp when you need one.

faqs.question: Do I need a licensed architect for drafting?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Drafting is unstamped work, and for many single-family and ADU projects under local size thresholds no licensed architect is required. If your specific submittal needs a stamp, we'll match you to a licensed pro for just that step.

faqs.question: What file formats do I get back?
faqs.answer: You receive editable CAD (DWG) plus flattened PDFs for printing and submittal. Layer standards can be matched to your or your builder's conventions on request.

faqs.question: How is hourly work kept honest?
faqs.answer: Every hour is tracked on-platform and visible to you, with escrow releasing against reviewed milestones — so there are no surprise invoices or padded time.

faqs.question: Can you work from just a hand sketch?
faqs.answer: Yes. A dimensioned sketch or even photos with measurements are enough to begin. The drafter will flag anything they need before starting.

faqs.question: Does it cost anything to join or receive leads?
faqs.answer: No. Joining is free, there's no monthly subscription, and you never pay to receive or view a matched lead. We only take a flat 10% service fee on projects you actually win.

faqs.question: How are leads matched to me?
faqs.answer: The engine matches on your verified license and jurisdiction, your chosen specialties and project types, and your current capacity. You see the pre-scoped, pre-priced project and accept or decline — nothing is ever assigned.

faqs.question: Do I set my own rates?
faqs.answer: Yes. You set a fixed quote or your hourly rate on every project. Clients see your number before they commit, and you can decline any lead that doesn't fit your pricing.

faqs.question: When do I get paid?
faqs.answer: Clients fund escrow when they hire you. As you complete each tracked milestone and the client approves it, the funds release to your bank — typically within two business days.

faqs.question: What do I need to apply?
faqs.answer: Your active state license, a short portfolio of past projects, your specialties and service area, your rates, and proof of errors & omissions insurance. Verification usually takes about three days.

faqs.question: Do I need to be a licensed architect to join?
faqs.answer: No. Most services on the platform — drafting, 3D visualization, scanning, and consults — need no license and can be delivered from anywhere. Only stamped, permit-ready work requires a professional licensed in the client's jurisdiction, so we verify credentials for those disciplines only.

faqs.question: What does it cost to join or receive orders?
faqs.answer: Nothing. Joining is free, there's no monthly subscription, and you never pay to receive or view a matched order. We take a flat 10% service fee only on orders you actually deliver.

faqs.question: How are orders matched to me?
faqs.answer: The engine matches on your discipline and specialties, your capacity, your rates, and — for stamped work — your verified license and jurisdiction. You see the scoped, priced order and accept or decline; nothing is ever assigned.

faqs.question: When and how do I get paid?
faqs.answer: Clients fund escrow when they place an order. As you deliver each milestone and the client approves it, funds release to your bank, typically within two business days.

faqs.question: What do I need to apply?
faqs.answer: A short portfolio of relevant work, your disciplines and rates, and your availability. Licensed disciplines (engineering, stamped permit work) also submit their license and insurance. Most reviews take about three days.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to design a ADU?
faqs.answer: A Backyard ADU drawing set typically runs $2,400 – $6,500 as a fixed quote, scaling with square footage and complexity. You see an itemized instant estimate before talking to anyone, and your architect confirms the number on your scoping call.

faqs.question: How long does the design take?
faqs.answer: Most Backyard ADU sets reach a stamped, permit-ready state in about 2–3 weeks of active design, depending on revision cycles and how quickly site info is provided.

faqs.question: Is the architect licensed for my area?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every match is verified as licensed in your state, and pre-cleared for Backyard ADU work in your jurisdiction, before it reaches you.

faqs.question: What do I need to provide?
faqs.answer: Basic site information, measurements or a recent survey, and photos. Your architect guides you through exactly what's needed — no in-person visit required.

faqs.question: Do I need an architect licensed specifically in CA?
faqs.answer: Yes. A permit-ready drawing set must be stamped by an architect licensed in the state where the project is built. Every match you receive is verified as licensed in CA before it reaches you.

faqs.question: How much does an architect cost in Oakland?
faqs.answer: It depends on scope. A backyard ADU set typically starts around $3,900, a home addition around $11,000, and a new custom home from $26,000. You get an itemized instant estimate before talking to anyone, and each architect confirms a fixed quote or hourly rate on your scoping call.

faqs.question: Can this really be done remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes. Site information, measurements, and photos are collected digitally, and Oakland plan-check submittals are handled electronically. You work with your architect over chat and video, and everything bills through escrow milestones.

faqs.question: How fast will I be matched?
faqs.answer: Within 48 hours of completing your free estimate you'll see 2–3 CA-licensed architects pre-cleared on jurisdiction experience and capacity for your project type.

faqs.question: Does my architect need to be licensed in California?
faqs.answer: Yes. A permit set must be stamped by an architect holding an active California license. Every match we surface for a California project is verified as actively licensed in the state before it reaches you.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a permit in California?
faqs.answer: Plan for roughly 8–14 weeks from scoping to an issued permit for a typical residential project — a few weeks of design plus 2–6 weeks of plan-check review, which varies by city and current backlog.

faqs.question: What is Title-24 and do I need it?
faqs.answer: Title-24 is California's energy-efficiency standard. Nearly every residential and commercial permit set must include Title-24 compliance documentation; your architect prepares it as part of the drawing set.

faqs.question: Why is California more expensive than other states?
faqs.answer: California scores 82/100 on our complexity index because of seismic, wildfire, Title-24 and — in many areas — coastal or historic review. That translates to a 1.35× pricing multiplier, applied automatically in your estimate.

faqs.question: Can I hire an architect remotely for a California project?
faqs.answer: Yes. The entire process — scoping, drawings, revisions and submission — runs on-platform with escrow-protected milestones. You never need an in-person meeting to reach a stamped, permit-ready set.
